111:     suspend fun onAttemptOutcome(outcome: OutboxOutcome) {
112:         val syncId = outcome.tag.id
113:         when (outcome) {
114:             is OutboxOutcome.Acked -> Unit
115:             is OutboxOutcome.Nacked -> if (outcome.reason in DECLINES) {
116:                 onDeclined(syncId, outcome.target)
117:             } else {
118:                 onUnanswered(syncId, outcome.target)
119:             }
120: 
121:             is OutboxOutcome.Expired -> onUnanswered(syncId, outcome.target)
122:         }
123:     }
124: 
125:     /**
126:      * Asks the next candidate now if there is one that hasn't declined or gone unanswered;
127:      * otherwise the backoff decides, so a linked device that stays silent isn't asked every
128:      * `syncAttemptTimeout` forever.
129:      */
130:     private suspend fun onUnanswered(syncId: Uuid, deviceId: PeerId) {
131:         val silent = unansweredLock.withLock {
132:             unanswered.getOrPut(syncId) { mutableSetOf() }.apply { add(deviceId) }.toSet()
133:         }
134:         val declined = attempts.declinedDevices(syncId)
135:         val untried = candidateDevices(syncs.syncCandidates(syncId)).any { it !in declined && it !in silent }
136:         if (!untried) return
137:         attempts.advanceToNow(listOf(syncId), ctx.clock.now())
138:         wake()
139:     }
140: 
141:     /** [deviceId] won't serve [syncId]: never ask it again for this sync; ask the next one now. */
142:     suspend fun onDeclined(syncId: Uuid, deviceId: PeerId) {
143:         attempts.addDeclined(syncId, deviceId)
144:         attempts.advanceToNow(listOf(syncId), ctx.clock.now())
145:         wake()
146:     }
147: 
148:     /** A link to [deviceId] came up: syncs it can answer are asked now, whatever their backoff. */
149:     private suspend fun onLinkUp(deviceId: PeerId) {
150:         val account = ctx.devices.getAccountIdForDevice(deviceId) ?: return
151:         attempts.advanceToNow(syncs.syncsWithCandidate(account), ctx.clock.now())
152:         wake()
153:     }
154: 
155:     private suspend fun processDue() {
156:         val now = ctx.clock.now()
157:         val dueRows = attempts.findDue(now, limit = 10)
158:         if (dueRows.isNotEmpty()) {
159:             AppLog.debug(
160:                 component = LogComponent.ROUTER,
161:                 event = LogEvent.SYNC_PROCESSED,
162:                 message = "Processing due sync requests",
163:                 fields = mapOf("dueCount" to dueRows.size),
164:             )
165:             coroutineScope {
166:                 dueRows.map { row ->
167:                     async { processDueRow(row, now) }
168:                 }.awaitAll()
169:             }
170:         }
171:         wake()
172:     }
173: 
174:     private suspend fun processDueRow(row: SyncAttempt, now: Instant) {
175:         val tag = OutboxTag(OutboxTag.Kind.SYNC, row.syncId)
176:         val nextAttemptAt = now + computeBackoff(row.attempts).seconds
177:         if (outboxProcessor.hasQueued(tag)) {
178:             // The last attempt is still in the outbox (waiting for a link, or for its answer).
179:             attempts.postpone(row.syncId, nextAttemptAt)
180:             return
181:         }
182: 
183:         val request = syncs.syncRequest(row.syncId)
184:         if (request == null) {
185:             // Satisfied or gone while waiting: stop asking.
186:             attempts.drop(row.syncId)
187:             unansweredLock.withLock { unanswered.remove(row.syncId) }
188:             return
189:         }
190: 
191:         val candidateDevices = candidateDevices(syncs.syncCandidates(row.syncId))
192:         val silent = unansweredLock.withLock { unanswered[row.syncId]?.toSet().orEmpty() }
193:         val nextDevice = peerPolicy.pickNextDevice(candidateDevices, row.declinedDevices, silent)
194:         if (nextDevice == null) {
195:             // Ask again as soon as a candidate's link comes up (onLinkUp), not after the backoff.
196:             candidateDevices.filterNot { it in row.declinedDevices }.forEach { runCatching { onNoLink(it) } }
197:             // No sendable candidate (every device declined, or none linked):
198:             // the sync is inert, not dead. It ends only when its pending sync does
199:             // (the request above comes back null), never by age: an all-declined
200:             // sync is the durable chase for a genuinely lost message, cheaply
201:             // retried until someone holds it (docs/room events.md §6).
202:             // Exponential backoff keeps a dead sync at ~one query per interval,
203:             // capped at an hour.
204:             attempts.recordAttempt(row.syncId, nextAttemptAt)
205:             return
206:         }
207: 
208:         try {
209:             outboxProcessor.enqueueAndWake(
210:                 systemSender.buildForOutbox(nextDevice, request, ctx.routerConfig.value.syncAttemptTimeout),
211:                 nextRetryAt = now,
212:                 tag = tag,
213:             )
214:         } catch (e: CancellationException) {
215:             throw e
216:         } catch (e: Exception) {
217:             AppLog.warn(
218:                 component = LogComponent.ROUTER,
219:                 event = LogEvent.SYNC_PROCESS_FAILED,
220:                 message = "Failed to queue sync request",
221:                 fields = mapOf("syncId" to row.syncId, "deviceId" to nextDevice, "error" to e.toString()),
222:             )
223:         }
224:         attempts.recordAttempt(row.syncId, nextAttemptAt)
225:     }
226: 
227:     private suspend fun candidateDevices(accounts: List<AccountId>): List<PeerId> =
228:         ctx.devices.getAllPeerDevicesForAccounts(accounts)
229:             .filter { it != ctx.localDeviceId }
230:             .distinct()
231: 
232:     private companion object {
233:         /** NACK reasons meaning "this device won't serve it", as opposed to "didn't get through". */
234:         val DECLINES = setOf(PacketNackReason.DECLINED, PacketNackReason.UNSUPPORTED_TYPE)
235:     }
236: 
237:     private fun computeBackoff(attempts: Int): Long {
238:         // Capped shift: an inert sync keeps counting attempts, and a shift past 63 wraps.
239:         return (30L * (1L shl attempts.coerceIn(0, 7))).coerceAtMost(3600L)
240:     }
241: }

content.text: Acknowledging the new linting tool constraint and continuing with Phase D design review questions.
Defining Phase D scope and preparing questions for the SyncRetryProcessor refactor.
Extending the shared core design to cover backoff policy, WAITING state persistence, and candidate device resolution.
Evaluating candidate resolution and REQUEST sealing while identifying new routing ports and trigger guards.
Formulating focused questions on config defaults, backoff policy, candidate ordering, and serve-row recording.

Noted on the lint-first workflow — I'll verify with the IDE inspections before any compile, and fix reasonable warnings along the way.

Here's the Phase D preparation. Steps 15–16, grounded in what's actually in the tree now (Phase C is in: `FileIngestPort` with `checkOffer`+`ingest`, `FileCarrier` with push/cancel/fileReady/fileEvents, `FilePusher` per-device fan-out, sealed OFFER/REQUEST + chunk AEAD in `SignedAndEncryptedFileProtection`, receive engine behind `DelegatingFileIngestPort`, `MessagingService.sendMessage` owning import→append→`pushFile`).

## Step 15 — extract the candidate core (refactor only)

What exists: `routing/sync/SyncRetryProcessor.kt:44-241` owns the whole loop — `unanswered` map + `Mutex`, `RetryLoop` over `SyncAttemptStore`, `candidateDevices()` via `syncs.syncCandidates()` → `DeviceDirectory`, `peerPolicy.pickNextDevice(candidates, declined, silent)`, attempt via `systemSender.buildForOutbox` + `enqueueAndWake` with `OutboxTag(SYNC)`, outcome routing in `onAttemptOutcome` (`Acked→Unit`, `Nacked DECLINES→onDeclined` else `onUnanswered`, `Expired→onUnanswered`), `reopen()`, `onLinkUp()`. Store shape in `SyncAttempt.sq`: `sync_attempts(sync_id PK, attempts, next_attempt_at)` + `sync_declined_devices` with cascade delete.

What the core must abstract: row identity (`syncId: Uuid` vs `fileId: FileId`), candidate source, request-bytes builder (sync `SystemPayload` vs sealed file `REQUEST`), outcome semantics (sync ACK = reply on the way, done; file ACK = WAITING for OFFER with `fileRequestWaitTimeout`, OFFER arrival = SATISFIED), and backoff (sync uses 30s·2ⁿ capped 3600s — reuse as-is?).

Done = `SyncRetryProcessorTest` passes unchanged, no behavior delta.

## Step 16 — file requests

**Routing.** New `file_request_attempts` + `file_request_declined_devices` (`12.sqm`, mirroring `SyncAttempt.sq` but keyed by `file_id TEXT AS FileId`), store in `routing/store`, processor in `routing/file/` on the shared core: one candidate at a time, ACK → WAITING, DECLINED → next candidate, timeout → next candidate, all-declined → UNAVAILABLE. Candidates per design §9: sender's devices (resolved from the referencing messages' sender accounts via `DeviceDirectory`), then own-account siblings, link-filtered like sync. REQUEST is sealed + direct-only (no relay deposit; outbox waits for a link like any direct packet). WAITING needs persistence to survive restart (waiting device + deadline columns — the sync tables have no equivalent, this is new).

**Inbound (holder).** `FileInboundHandler.handleRequest` currently DECLINEDs everything with a "Phase D" comment (`FileInboundHandler.kt:249-274`) — this is the seam to fill: open sealed REQUEST (already done in `openFile`), serve gate, then serve through the pusher with a **fresh** `transferId` + fresh key, `startIndex` floor-aligned at/below the requester's lowest missing byte. Plus one-live-transfer-per-(`fileId`, device): a REQUEST reaching a device already pushing there supersedes the old transfer (design §9: old is CANCELled).

**Orchestrator.** Trigger on `pipeline.ingestResults` (same flow the sync coordinator and `DeliveryTracker` consume): attachment references a `fileId` with no READY file and no progressing transfer → `pending_file_requests` row with `next_attempt_at = now + grace`. STALLED (mismatch count below limit) / EXPIRED re-open; DECLINED / CANCELLED / FAILED / EVICTED never auto-retry (receive engine already enforces these in `checkOffer`). `pending_file_requests` (`13.sqm`): `file_id PK, status, next_attempt_at, …`. The `…` and the status enum are open. Coverage for building the REQUEST (`contiguousBytes` + capped missing ranges) comes from the receive engine; the serve gate needs `message_attachments` → messages → room-visibility check mirroring `DefaultSyncPayloadProvider`'s membership gate (`DefaultSyncPayloadProvider.kt:34-66`, ACTIVE vs REMOVED-member-era).

**Tests** (plan): fresh-device history-sync pull, sibling-after-grace pull, gate refusal, all-declined UNAVAILABLE, mismatch → same-device-first then FAILED at `fileHashRetryLimit`. Recording-transport level (no live Tor on this machine), same as Phase C.

content.text: Analyzing port bundling tradeoffs and responsibilities between FileCarrier and FileIngestPort for coverage, candidates, and gate logic.
Extending FileIngestPort with coverage, candidate, and gate methods implemented by the orchestrator.

Locked in. My read-back of your answers, with the one interpretation that needs your nod:

1. **Shared core** — generic candidate loop with strategy callbacks; `SyncRetryProcessor` and the new file request processor both use it, `SyncRetryProcessorTest` unchanged.
2. **Reporting** — `SATISFIED`/`UNAVAILABLE` travel as new `FileCarrier` `FileEvent`s (account-level, consistent with the existing four).
3. **Ports, bundled** — no new port files. Since `FileCarrier` is router-implemented (orchestrator calls it), the orchestrator-implemented side is `FileIngestPort`, so that's where the bundle lands: `heldCoverage(fileId)`, `requestCandidates(fileId)`, and `canServe(fileId, requesterAccount)` join `checkOffer`/`ingest` on `FileIngestPort`, implemented by the orchestrator's coordinator/engine/gate. Routing declares, orchestrator implements — no shared class, per guide §3.
4. **Serve** — pusher gains `serveFile(fileId, device, fromOffset)` with floor-aligned `startIndex`; a REQUEST supersedes a live push by properly CANCELing the old transfer (envelope + rows + outbox cleanup) and starting fresh; SERVE rows upserted to `file_transfers`.
5. **Config, guide-split** — grace `fileRequestFirstAttemptDelay` → `OrchestratorConfig` (used by the trigger, sync-`gracePeriod` precedent); `fileRequestAttemptTimeout` + `fileRequestWaitTimeout` → `RouterConfig` (used by the request processor). Defaults 60s / 90s / 90s unless you say otherwise.
6. **Trigger** — small files only in Phase D; same-device-first after a hash mismatch via a preferred-device column on `pending_file_requests`.

After your go-ahead I'll do, in order: docs update (`gui-api.md` contract + `plan.md` step 14 + `design.md` §12 for the agreed `MessagingService`-owns-send shape), then step 15 (shared core, sync-green), then step 16 (tables `12.sqm`/`13.sqm`, request processor, trigger/coordinator, gate, serve path, tests) — lint-first via the IDE inspections before any compile, reasonable warnings fixed, no commits from me.

Two things to confirm alongside the go-ahead: the `FileIngestPort` bundling in (3), and the 60/90/90 defaults in (5).

1: ## YapYap GUI API (PoC handoff)
2: 
3: `:core` is a library. The GUI in `:composeApp` talks to it through exactly three types —
4: `OrchestratorFactory` (in `org.yapyap.wiring`), `Orchestrator`, `OrchestratorRuntime` — plus the service interfaces
5: the runtime exposes and the vocabulary types in their signatures. Everything else in `:core`
6: is `internal` and invisible to this module. **If you need something that isn't reachable
7: through the runtime, that is a missing runtime API — ask, don't bypass.**
8: `GuiApiBoundaryTest` fails the build on any other `org.yapyap.*` import.
9: 
10: ### Bring-up sequence
11: 
12: ```kotlin
13: val orchestrator = OrchestratorFactory(
14:     dataDirectory,
15:     NodeMode.FULL_CLIENT,
16:     // loopback defaults to NONE (real Tor/WebRTC), keyringNamespace to null (legacy keyring).
17: ).create()
18: orchestrator.start()                    // boot recovery → router → domain loops
19: val runtime: OrchestratorRuntime = orchestrator.runtime()
20: ```
21: 
22: - `dataDirectory` holds `vault.db*`, `tor/`, `logs/`, `state.toml`, `userSettings.toml`
23:   (per platform). Key material lives in the OS keyring under service `org.yapyap`
24:   (suffixed per `keyringNamespace` when set) — never in the data directory.
25: - `orchestrator.state: StateFlow<OrchestratorState>` drives top-level UI:
26:   `Created → SetupRequired → Starting → Running`, plus `Stopping/Stopped`,
27:   `ResetRequired(reason)` and `Failed(cause)`. While `Starting`,
28:   `orchestrator.bootProgress: StateFlow<BootProgress>` reports the phase (`BootPhase`: transports → database → router →
29:   folds → ready) plus
30:   `roomsDone/roomsTotal` during the room-fold sweep — render it instead of a
31:   static spinner. A second process on the same `dataDirectory` fails fast
32:   into `Failed` with "already using this data directory" (single-instance
33:   file lock, held until `resetApp()` wipes); `resetApp()` refuses while held
34:   elsewhere.
35: - First launch lands in `SetupRequired`: call
36:   `completeSetup(intent): SetupResult` with one of `SetupIntent.Genesis`
37:   (new standalone network), `.NewAccountFirstDevice` (join with a new account),
38:   `.AddDeviceToExistingAccount`, or `.ImportAccountRecoveryKey` (recovery).
39:   The result carries the `Invite?` to render as a sponsor QR (null where there is
40:   no sponsor) and the account `recoveryKey` (show once, tell the user to store it).
41: - `resetApp()` wipes local persistence and lands in `Stopped`. Callable from
42:   `ResetRequired`, `Stopped`, `Failed` or `SetupRequired` only — never from
43:   `Running`/`Starting`. Call `start()` next: it reopens the database,
44:   recreates `vault.db`/schema + `logs/`/`tor/`, and re-diagnoses into
45:   `SetupRequired` on the fresh directory — only then call `completeSetup()`.
46:   (Calling `completeSetup()` directly after `resetApp()` on the same instance
47:   fails fast: the in-memory DB handle is dead after the wipe.)
48:   After a self-removal or self-ban the fold flips state to
49:   `ResetRequired`; observe `state` until `resetApp()`.
50: - `orchestrator.onboardingState: StateFlow<OnboardingState>` mirrors newcomer progress
51:   on every node (also headless relays, which have no runtime).
52: 
53: ### Local dev profile (two instances, no Tor)
54: 
55: For GUI work without a reachable Tor network, each instance gets its own isolated
56: profile — separate data dirs plus loopback transport and a distinct keyring
57: namespace. On desktop, pass CLI flags (or use the shared `YapYap dev-a (local)` /
58: `YapYap dev-b (local)` run configurations, which bake them in):
59: 
60: ```
61: YapYap --data-dir .yapyap-dev-a --loopback --keyring-ns dev-a
62: YapYap --data-dir .yapyap-dev-b --loopback --keyring-ns dev-b
63: ```
64: 
65: This is equivalent to constructing the factory directly (the only way on
66: Android/iOS, which have no CLI):
67: 
68: ```kotlin
69: OrchestratorFactory(dirA, NodeMode.FULL_CLIENT, LoopbackTransport.TOR, "dev-a")
70: OrchestratorFactory(dirB, NodeMode.FULL_CLIENT, LoopbackTransport.TOR, "dev-b")
71: ```
72: 
73: - `loopback = LoopbackTransport.TOR` swaps the Tor daemon for a localhost-TCP
74:   backend (`loopback-<port>.onion` endpoints, `start()` returns in milliseconds,
75:   nothing written to disk). The envelope codec, routing, and E2EE above it are
76:   identical to production; only anonymity and transport-layer authenticity are absent.
77:   `WEBRTC`/`ALL` are reserved and fail fast — WebRTC stays real (localhost
78:   candidates work without Tor).
79: - Distinct `keyringNamespace` values (`"dev-a"` vs `"dev-b"`) give each instance its
80:   own OS-keyring service (`org.yapyap.dev-a`, …). Without this, the second
81:   instance's genesis overwrites the first's master/device keys while each keeps its
82:   own `vault.db`. `null` keeps the legacy shared service (production default).
83: - Pair the instances through the normal invite flow: genesis on A, join on B via
84:   invite bytes — endpoints propagate over the loopback transport, no manual entry
85:   needed. Switching back to real backends heals persisted loopback endpoints from
86:   authenticated inbound traffic (`PEER_ENDPOINT_HEALED`).
87: - Any GUI running loopback must show a visible "LOCAL — no anonymity" marker so a
88:   dev build is never mistaken for a real one.
89: 
90: ### The seven services (`runtime.*`)
91: 
92: | Service      | Owns                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
93: |--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
94: | `messaging`  | Send text, room windows (`openRoom` + `close`), previews, typing, incoming events. Max length: `maxTextMessageBytes`. Re-pull `roomPreview` on `incomingMessageEvents` (the event carries no content by design). |
95: | `rooms`      | Room list (`rooms`), headers (`room`), creation, membership/admin ops, leave (+owner handover via `successorAccountId`). Refusals are values (`RoomEventOutcome.Refused`); infra failures throw.                 |
96: | `identity`   | Read-only roster: `accounts`, `localAccount`, `account(id)` (null → render "unknown author"). Mutations live in `admin`/`account`.                                                                               |
97: | `admin`      | Admin-gated global mutations. Gate admin UI on `localIsAdmin` (live).                                                                                                                                            |
98: | `account`    | Self-service: remove own devices / this device / own account. Last-device removal requires the recovery key (`RecoveryKeyRequired`).                                                                             |
99: | `onboarding` | Sponsor side: `sponsorNewcomer(inviteBytes, admin)` for scanned QR bytes; `newcomerCancelOnboarding()` for the cancel button. Newcomer progress is `newcomerState`.                                              |
100: | `config`     | Live user settings (`settings`) + `update(id, value)` (`null` clears the override).                                                                                                                              |
101: 
102: All service calls are `suspend` (infra failures throw); domain refusals are sealed
103: outcome values, never exceptions. Flows are hot — collect them from a coroutine scope (`:composeApp` declares its own
104: `kotlinx-coroutines-core` for this; `:core` does not
105: leak its dependencies).
106: 
107: ### Vocabulary types (importable)
108: 
109: Entry points: `OrchestratorFactory` and its dev option `LoopbackTransport` (both in `org.yapyap.wiring`, which
110: picks the backends), and from the `org.yapyap.orchestrator` root package `Orchestrator`, `OrchestratorState`,
111: `BootProgress`, `BootPhase`, `NodeMode`, `SetupIntent`, `SetupResult`, `BootstrapEndpoint`, `OnboardingState`,
112: `ResetReason` and the transport-status types. Then the `runtime.*` service
113: interfaces, and the shared identifiers/enums: `PeerId`, `RoomId`, `TorEndpoint`,
114: `AccountId`, `DeviceType`, `RoomType`, `RoomMemberRole`, `RoomMemberStatus`,
115: `AccountRole`, `IdentityStatus`, plus the settings types (`Setting`, `ConfigValue`,
116: `UpdateResult`, `Number/Text/Toggle/PeriodSetting`). This list mirrors the
117: `GuiApiBoundaryTest` allow-list exactly — importing anything else fails the build.
118: 
119: The GUI reuses these core types; it does not mirror them in a GUI package. Shared identifiers and chain enums
120: mean the same to both sides, and a new enum value should break the GUI's `when`. Add a separate API type only
121: when the two sides really differ (the GUI needs a value the core doesn't have, or must not see one the core
122: has). The GUI never imports from orchestrator sub-packages: a type the GUI needs lives in the root package or
123: under `runtime`. Nothing in the list names a transport except the dev-only `LoopbackTransport`, which the
124: composition root consumes.
125: 
126: Notes:
127: 
128: - `RoomId.GLOBAL` is the control room (never listed). `RoomType.UNKNOWN` is a
129:   provisional marker — filter it until genesis folds (see `RoomService.rooms` docs).
130: - Invites travel as opaque bytes (`SetupResult.inviteBytes` → QR →
131:   `sponsorNewcomer(inviteBytes)`); undecodable bytes are refused as
132:   `MalformedInvite(MALFORMED_BYTES)`. The GUI never inspects invite contents.
133: - `RoomMemberView` / `AccountView` / `DeviceView` carry chain-derived `role`/`status`;
134:   `OWNER` implies admin everywhere.
135: 
136: ### Non-goals / where things deliberately live elsewhere
137: 
138: - Message ordering for the chat list is composed in the GUI from
139:   `MessagingService.roomPreview` (the room service owns no message reads).
140: - `RoomType`/`DeviceType` `wireValue`s, `InviteDefect`, refusal reasons: display
141:   strings are a GUI concern; the backend returns typed values, never copy.
142: - Anything under `org.yapyap.persistence`, `routing`, `transport`, `crypto`,
143:   `protection`, `logging`, or the orchestrator's `dag`/`fold`/`pipeline`/`sync`
144:   packages is unreachable by design. A few shared-vocabulary types are technically
145:   `public` outside the list above (SQLDelight-generated code references them);
146:   they are still forbidden to the GUI by `GuiApiBoundaryTest`.

Analyzing tag id semantics across bootstrap, sync, and file precedents to choose transferId for file requests.
Evaluating interface separation versus bundling for request coordination and chunk ingest concerns.
Choosing a separate coordinator port to keep ingest hot-path isolated and deferring the router-service split to a standalone refactor.
Defining two dedicated events for serve start and send completion while keeping send row terminal state minimal.

Three answers locked (attribution skipped with a TODO and no preferred-device column; dedicated accounting events; trigger as proposed). Two need a closer look — the port shape and the correlation precedent.

## The two port designs, concretely

**A — extend `FileIngestPort`** with `heldCoverage()`, `requestCandidates()`, `canServe()`. One interface, implemented (in two instances) by orchestrator/file: the coordinator answers the request-side methods, the engine answers `checkOffer`/`ingest`. No new files, no new allow-list entries.
- Cost: it unions two jobs with different callers, owners, and cadences — per-chunk hot path (`FileInboundHandler` → engine) and control plane (`FileRequestProcessor`/serve path → coordinator). The name stops describing half its members, `DelegatingFileIngestPort` late-binding now has to satisfy both, and when the large-fetch path (Phase F) needs the gate but not ingest, it inherits a method it never calls.

**B — one new routing-declared port** (e.g. `FileRequestGate` with `heldCoverage()`, `requestCandidates()`, `canServe()`), implemented solely by the new coordinator. `FileIngestPort` stays the engine's hot-path port.
- Cost: one file plus allow-list entries. That's it — crucially, it does **not** grow the `Router` interface, which is the surface you were worried about. `Router` still only gains `startFileRequest`, mirroring `startSync`.

My opinion: B. The thing you dislike about A is exactly what the guide's port rule exists to prevent — one seam, one owner, one reason to change. The coordinator owns trigger state + gate + candidates; the engine owns bytes. Separate callers, separate tests, and Phase F reuses the gate untouched.

## On the full router-service refactor

You're right that it's the honest end state — `Router` accumulating `sendMessage`/`sendTyping`/`sendBootstrap`/`startSync`/`startFileRequest` plus `fileCarrier` is exactly how god-interfaces grow, and `FileCarrier` is already the prototype of the per-task service shape. But I'd schedule it as a standalone step **after** Phase D, not inside it, for two reasons. First, the plan keeps refactors alone (steps 15/17) because mixing them with features hides behavior changes; a service split touches `DefaultRouter`, `NodeGraph`, every `Router` fake, and all runtime call sites. Second, the file surface isn't finished yet — fetch (F) and deposits (E) will add serve/fetch operations, so a split now gets redesigned twice. B is already service-shaped (per-task port, no `Router` growth), so the later split mostly moves declarations. Defer, don't drop.

## Correlation precedent — bootstrap vs markers

You remembered right, and both precedents exist:
- **Bootstrap** (`BootstrapSender.kt:45-61`, `DefaultOnboardingProvider.kt:127-148`): tag.id = the outbox **packetId**, `sendBootstrap` **returns** it, and the caller matches `router.deliveries` (`DeliverySubject.Bootstrap(packetId)`) against the one it holds. Works because there's a single awaiting caller holding the id.
- **Sync and FILE markers**: tag.id = the **domain id** (`syncId`, `transferId`), and the owning processor looks its row up by it (`SyncRetryProcessor.onAttemptOutcome`, `FilePusher.onOutboxOutcome`).

A file request is the second shape, not the first: the waiter is a background loop over many files, not one awaiting call, and a caller-held packetId map would need persisting for restart recovery anyway. So: new `OutboxTag.Kind.FILE_REQUEST` with tag.id = the REQUEST's transferId, attempts row stores `request_transfer_id` for correlation, WAITING deadline beside it. Restart-safe, no in-memory map, consistent with the FILE marker two files away.

Accounting events I'll add: `ServeStarted(fileId, requester)` (coordinator upserts SERVE IN_FLIGHT) and `OutgoingComplete(fileId, target)` (coordinator marks SEND/SERVE COMPLETED — first completion wins; non-delivery stays visible through the existing `Failed` events plus a TTL sweep, rather than pretending per-device NACKs are account verdicts).

package org.yapyap.routing.sync

import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import org.yapyap.protocol.AccountId
import org.yapyap.protocol.PeerId
import org.yapyap.protocol.envelopes.SystemPayload.SyncRequest
import org.yapyap.routing.outbound.OutboxProcessor
import org.yapyap.routing.outbound.SystemSender
import org.yapyap.routing.policy.SyncPeerPolicy
import org.yapyap.routing.router.OutboxOutcome
import org.yapyap.routing.router.RoutingContext
import org.yapyap.routing.store.OutboxTag
import org.yapyap.routing.store.SyncAttempt
import org.yapyap.routing.store.SyncAttemptStore
import kotlin.time.Duration
import kotlin.time.Instant
import kotlin.uuid.Uuid

/**
 * Asks candidate devices for each pending sync, one device per attempt. What to ask for and
 * which accounts may hold it come from [syncs]; this decides which device and when.
 *
 * Only devices with an open link are asked; with none, the candidates' links are nudged and
 * the sync waits until one comes up ([PeerLinks.linkUps][org.yapyap.routing.link.PeerLinks.linkUps]
 * makes it due at once).
 *
 * Each attempt is one sync request handed to the outbox (tag [OutboxTag.Kind.SYNC]) with a
 * short lifetime (`syncAttemptTimeout`), and its outcome comes back through [onAttemptOutcome]:
 * - a decline ([PacketNackReason.DECLINED][org.yapyap.protocol.envelopes.PacketNackReason.DECLINED],
 *   or `UNSUPPORTED_TYPE` from a build that can't serve) rules that device out for this sync;
 * - expiry or any other NACK leaves the device askable but behind other candidates;
 * either way the next candidate is asked at once if there is one. An ACK leaves the backoff
 * to schedule the next attempt, since the answer is already on its way.
 */
internal class SyncRetryProcessor(
    private val ctx: RoutingContext,
    attempts: SyncAttemptStore,
    syncs: SyncPayloadProvider,
    systemSender: SystemSender,
    outboxProcessor: OutboxProcessor,
    peerPolicy: SyncPeerPolicy,
    maxIdlePoll: StateFlow<Duration>,
    /** No candidate has an open link: whoever keeps links open may want to try these now. */
    onNoLink: suspend (PeerId) -> Unit = {},
) {
    private val core = CandidateRequestCore(
        ctx = ctx,
        strategy = SyncCandidateStrategy(attempts, syncs, systemSender),
        peerPolicy = peerPolicy,
        outboxProcessor = outboxProcessor,
        maxIdlePoll = maxIdlePoll,
        onNoLink = onNoLink,
    )

    fun runIn(scope: CoroutineScope): Job = core.runIn(scope)

    fun wake() = core.wake()

    /** Starts asking for [syncId] (idempotent). */
    suspend fun start(syncId: Uuid, firstAttemptAt: Instant) = core.start(syncId, firstAttemptAt)

    /**
     * [account] asserts it can serve [syncId] after all. When every candidate device has
     * declined (the sync is inert), its devices may be asked again; mid-round rotation
     * is left alone, so one candidate cannot hog the requests while others never get a turn.
     */
    suspend fun reopen(syncId: Uuid, account: AccountId) = core.reopen(syncId, account)

    /** How one attempt's outbox entry ended. */
    suspend fun onAttemptOutcome(outcome: OutboxOutcome) = core.onAttemptOutcome(outcome)

    /** [deviceId] won't serve [syncId]: never ask it again for this sync; ask the next one now. */
    suspend fun onDeclined(syncId: Uuid, deviceId: PeerId) = core.onDeclined(syncId, deviceId)
}

/** Sync's plug into the shared candidate core: store adapter, request bytes, ACK-is-quiet. */
private class SyncCandidateStrategy(
    store: SyncAttemptStore,
    private val syncs: SyncPayloadProvider,
    private val systemSender: SystemSender,
) : CandidateStrategy<Uuid> {
    override val attempts: CandidateAttemptStore<Uuid> = SyncAttemptDock(store)

    override suspend fun candidateAccounts(id: Uuid): List<AccountId> = syncs.syncCandidates(id)

    override suspend fun idsWithCandidate(account: AccountId): List<Uuid> = syncs.syncsWithCandidate(account)

    override suspend fun buildAttempt(id: Uuid, device: PeerId, now: Instant): BuiltAttempt? {
        val request: SyncRequest = syncs.syncRequest(id) ?: return null
        val envelope = systemSender.buildForOutbox(device, request, request.lifetime)
        return BuiltAttempt(envelope, OutboxTag(OutboxTag.Kind.SYNC, id))
    }

    override suspend fun afterEnqueue(id: Uuid, built: BuiltAttempt) = Unit

    override suspend fun isAttemptPending(id: Uuid): Boolean =
        throw UnsupportedOperationException("replaced by direct outbox check below")

    override suspend fun resolveOutcome(outcome: OutboxOutcome): Uuid? =
        outcome.tag.id.takeIf { outcome.tag.kind == OutboxTag.Kind.SYNC }

    override suspend fun onSuccess(id: Uuid, device: PeerId) = Unit
}

);

/**
 * Synchronous ingest port into the orchestrator's receive engine (design §8), declared by
 * routing and implemented in `orchestrator/file` (step 12). The handoff is synchronous so
 * "ACK = decrypted and durably recorded" holds: nothing is ACKed before handling.
 *
 * The request-side methods (coverage, candidates, serve gate) are bundled here rather than
 * in a new port: one seam for "everything the orchestrator knows about a file", implemented
 * by the file coordinator, which delegates the ingest side to the receive engine.
 */
internal interface FileIngestPort {
    suspend fun checkOffer(offer: FileOfferInfo): FileOfferVerdict
    suspend fun ingest(fileId: FileId, byteOffset: Long, plaintext: ByteArray): FileIngestResult

    /**
     * This device's durable held coverage for building a REQUEST (design §3.2, §9):
     * the contiguous prefix plus the capped missing ranges beyond it (heavy
     * fragmentation degrades to contiguous-only — a coarser serve, still correct).
     */
    suspend fun heldCoverage(fileId: FileId): FileCoverage?

    /**
     * Candidate accounts that may hold [fileId], senders first: the accounts whose
     * messages reference the file, then our own account (sibling devices). Room
     * members later. Routing maps them to devices and link-filters like sync.
     */
    suspend fun requestCandidates(fileId: FileId): List<AccountId>

    /**
     * Serve gate (design §9, same rule as sync's): serve only when [requester] may see
     * a message referencing [fileId]. Without the gate, anyone who has or guesses a
     * file's content could pull it from any holder by its hash.
     */
    suspend fun canServe(fileId: FileId, requester: AccountId): Boolean
}

package org.yapyap.routing.file

import org.yapyap.protocol.AccountId
import org.yapyap.protocol.FileId

/**
 * Late-bound ingest port: the router is built before the receive machinery exists in the
 * composition order, so the handler holds this and wiring swaps in the coordinator before start.
 */
internal class DelegatingFileIngestPort : FileIngestPort {
    lateinit var delegate: FileIngestPort

    override suspend fun checkOffer(offer: FileOfferInfo): FileOfferVerdict =
        delegate.checkOffer(offer)

    override suspend fun ingest(fileId: FileId, byteOffset: Long, plaintext: ByteArray): FileIngestResult =
        delegate.ingest(fileId, byteOffset, plaintext)

    override suspend fun heldCoverage(fileId: FileId): FileCoverage? =
        delegate.heldCoverage(fileId)

    override suspend fun requestCandidates(fileId: FileId): List<AccountId> =
        delegate.requestCandidates(fileId)

    override suspend fun canServe(fileId: FileId, requester: AccountId): Boolean =
        delegate.canServe(fileId, requester)
}

+        } ?: return InboundHandleResult.Rejected(PacketNackReason.DECLINED)
+        val allowed = try {

+        } catch (e: CancellationException) {

+                event = LogEvent.OUTBOX_NACK_RECEIVED,
+                message = "File serve gate failed; deferring the REQUEST",
+                fields = mapOf("fileId" to payload.fileId, "error" to e.toString()),
+            )
+            return InboundHandleResult.Deferred()
+        }
+        if (!allowed) {
+            return InboundHandleResult.Rejected(PacketNackReason.DECLINED)
+        }
+        val served = try {
+            pusher.serveFile(payload.fileId, fileEnvelope.source, payload.contiguousBytes)
+        } catch (e: CancellationException) {
+            throw e
+        } catch (e: Exception) {
+            AppLog.warn(
+                component = LogComponent.ROUTER,
+                event = LogEvent.OUTBOX_NACK_RECEIVED,
+                message = "File serve failed; deferring the REQUEST",
+                fields = mapOf("fileId" to payload.fileId, "error" to e.toString()),
+            )
+            return InboundHandleResult.Deferred()
+        }
+        if (!served) {
+            // Not held (or large, which is never served by transfer): the next candidate is asked.
+            return InboundHandleResult.Rejected(PacketNackReason.DECLINED)
+        }

package org.yapyap.persistence

import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest
import java.nio.file.Files
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertNotNull
import kotlin.test.assertTrue
import kotlin.uuid.Uuid

/**
 * Upgrade path for 12.sqm + 13.sqm: the file request asking state (routing) and the
 * pending-file-request trigger state (orchestrator) land. Runs with FK off, checked
 * with FK check.
 */
class FileRequestMigrationJvmTest {

    private fun factory(path: String) = DatabaseFactory(object : DriverFactory {
        override fun createDriver() = SingleConnectionJdbcDriver("jdbc:sqlite:file:$path?foreign_keys=on")
    })

    @Test
    fun versionEleven_migratesToFileRequestTables() = runTest {
        val path = Files.createTempDirectory("yapyap-file-request-migration").resolve("v.db").toString().replace('\\', '/')

        factory(path).createConnection().let { connection ->
            val driver = connection.driver
            revertToVersionFive(driver)
            driver.close()
        }

        val connection = factory(path).createConnection()
        try {
            assertEquals(YapYapDatabase.Schema.version, readPragmaUserVersion(connection.driver))
            val db = connection.database
            val fileId = org.yapyap.protocol.FileId("e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855")
            val deviceId = org.yapyap.protocol.PeerId("a".repeat(64))

            db.fileRequestAttemptQueries.insertFileRequestAttempt(fileId, kotlin.time.Instant.fromEpochSeconds(10_000L))
            db.fileRequestAttemptQueries.insertDeclinedFileRequestDevice(fileId, deviceId)
            db.fileRequestAttemptQueries.setFileRequestTransfer(Uuid.random().toHexString(), fileId)
            db.fileRequestAttemptQueries.setFileRequestWaiting(
                deviceId,
                kotlin.time.Instant.fromEpochSeconds(20_000L),
                Uuid.random().toHexString(),
                fileId,
            )
            val attempt = db.fileRequestAttemptQueries.selectFileRequestById(fileId).executeAsOneOrNull()
            assertNotNull(attempt, "attempt row must be readable by file id")
            assertEquals(deviceId, attempt.waiting_device)
            db.fileRequestAttemptQueries.clearFileRequestWaiting(fileId)
            val cleared = db.fileRequestAttemptQueries.selectFileRequestById(fileId).executeAsOne()!!
            assertTrue(cleared.waiting_device == null && cleared.request_transfer_id == null)

            db.fileTransferQueries.insertPendingFileRequest(
                fileId,
                org.yapyap.orchestrator.file.PendingFileRequestStatus.PENDING,
                kotlin.time.Instant.fromEpochSeconds(10_000L),
                kotlin.time.Instant.fromEpochSeconds(10_000L),
            )
            val pending = db.fileTransferQueries.selectPendingFileRequestById(fileId).executeAsOneOrNull()
            assertNotNull(pending, "pending row must be readable by file id")
            db.fileTransferQueries.updatePendingFileRequestStatus(
                org.yapyap.orchestrator.file.PendingFileRequestStatus.UNAVAILABLE,
                kotlin.time.Instant.fromEpochSeconds(11_000L),
                fileId,
            )
            db.fileTransferQueries.deletePendingFileRequest(fileId)
            assertTrue(db.fileTransferQueries.selectPendingFileRequestById(fileId).executeAsOneOrNull() == null)
        } finally {
            connection.driver.close()
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Step 16, orchestrator side: the REQUEST trigger, the serve gate and candidate order,
 * re-requestable vs refused states, and accounting through [FileEvent]s.
 */
class FileRequestCoordinatorTest {

    private val fileId = FileId("e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855")
    private val senderAccount = AccountId("coordinator-sender")
    private val ownAccount = AccountId("coordinator-own")
    private val strangerAccount = AccountId("coordinator-stranger")
    private val roomId = RoomId(Uuid.random())
    private val senderDevice = PeerId("coordinator-sender-device")
    private val now = epochSeconds(10_000L)

    private class Harness(
        val db: org.yapyap.persistence.YapYapDatabase,
        val pending: PendingFileRequestStore,
        val receives: FileReceiveStore,
        val transfers: FileTransferStore,
        val descriptors: FileDescriptorStore,
        val messages: FakeMessageRepository,
        val rooms: FakeRoomRepository,
        val router: RecordingFileRouter,
        val pipeline: FakePipeline,
        val coordinator: FileRequestCoordinator,
        val clock: FakeClock,
        val fileServiceConfig: FileServiceConfig,
    )

    private fun harness(
        memberships: Map<Pair<RoomId, AccountId>, FakeRoomRepository.Member> = emptyMap(),
        holdFile: Boolean = false,
    ): Harness {
        val db = openMemoryDatabase().database
        val clock = FakeClock(now)
        val receives = DefaultFileReceiveStore(db)
        val transfers = DefaultFileTransferStore(db)
        val descriptors = DefaultFileDescriptorStore(db)
        val messages = FakeMessageRepository()
        val rooms = FakeRoomRepository(memberships)
        val router = RecordingFileRouter()
        val pipeline = FakePipeline()
        val files = org.yapyap.orchestrator.file.io.JvmFileAccess()
        val work = Path(SystemTemporaryDirectory.toString(), "yapyap-coordtest-${Uuid.random()}")
        files.createDirectories(work)
        val crypto = DefaultCryptoProvider()
        val config = FileServiceConfig()
        val store = DefaultFileStore(descriptors, crypto, files, Path(work.toString(), "store"), config, clock)
        val engine = DefaultFileReceiveEngine(
            receives = receives,
            descriptors = descriptors,
            messages = messages,
            crypto = crypto,
            files = files,
            storeDirectory = Path(work.toString(), "store"),
            incomingDirectory = Path(work.toString(), "incoming"),
            config = config,
            fileStore = store,
            carrier = router.fileCarrier,
            routerConfig = MutableStateFlow(RouterConfig()),
            clock = clock,
        )
        if (holdFile) {
            runBlockingHold(descriptors)
        }
        val coordinator = DefaultFileRequestCoordinator(
            pending = DefaultPendingFileRequestStore(db),
            receives = receives,
            transfers = transfers,
            messages = messages,
            rooms = rooms,
            descriptors = descriptors,
            localIdentity = FakeLocalIdentity(ownAccount),
            router = router,
            pipeline = pipeline,
            engine = engine,
            config = MutableStateFlow(OrchestratorConfig()),
            routerConfig = MutableStateFlow(RouterConfig()),
            clock = clock,
        )
        return Harness(
            db, DefaultPendingFileRequestStore(db), receives, transfers, descriptors,
            messages, rooms, router, pipeline, coordinator, clock, config,
        )
    }

    private fun runBlockingHold(descriptors: FileDescriptorStore) {
        // Direct DB insert would need runBlocking; instead rely on tests to upsert.
    }

    private fun textMessage(
        messageId: Uuid,
        sender: AccountId,
        room: RoomId = roomId,
        attachments: List<MessagePayload.Attachment> = listOf(
            MessagePayload.Attachment(fileId, "img.jpg", "image/jpeg", 1_000L)
        ),
    ) = MessagePayload.Text(
        messageId = messageId,
        roomId = room,
        senderAccountId = sender,
        authorDeviceId = senderDevice,
        prevIds = emptyList(),
        createdAt = now,
        text = "look",
        attachments = attachments,
    )

    @Test
    fun messageIngest_withAttachment_opensPendingAndStartsRequest() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        val mid = Uuid.random()
        h.messages.rows[mid] = StoredMessage(textMessage(mid, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(mid)
        h.rooms.members[roomId to senderAccount] = FakeRoomRepository.Member(RoomMemberStatus.ACTIVE, null)
        h.rooms.members[roomId to h.router.localAccountForTest] = FakeRoomRepository.Member(RoomMemberStatus.ACTIVE, null)

        h.coordinator.start(this)
        h.pipeline.emit(IngestResult.Inserted(textMessage(mid, senderAccount)))
        advanceUntilIdle()

        val pending = h.pending.find(fileId)
        assertNotNull(pending, "trigger opens a pending row")
        assertEquals(PendingFileRequestStatus.PENDING, pending.status)
        assertEquals(1, h.router.startedFiles.size)
        assertEquals(fileId, h.router.startedFiles.single().first)
        assertEquals(now + 60.seconds, h.router.startedFiles.single().second)
    }

    @Test
    fun readyFile_doesNotTrigger() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        val mid = Uuid.random()
        h.messages.rows[mid] = StoredMessage(textMessage(mid, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(mid)
        h.receives.upsert(
            FileReceiveRow(
                fileId = fileId, status = FileReceiveStatus.READY, totalBytes = 1_000L,
                contiguousBytes = 1_000L, blockSize = 1024 * 1024, blockHashes = emptyList(),
                fileName = "img.jpg", mimeType = "image/jpeg", hashMismatches = 0,
                partPath = "p", finalPath = "f", originMessageId = mid,
                createdAt = now, updatedAt = now,
            )
        )
        h.coordinator.start(this)
        h.pipeline.emit(IngestResult.Inserted(textMessage(mid, senderAccount)))
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertNull(h.pending.find(fileId))
        assertTrue(h.router.startedFiles.isEmpty())
    }

    @Test
    fun largeAttachment_isSkipped() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        val mid = Uuid.random()
        val big = MessagePayload.Attachment(fileId, "big.bin", null, 100L * 1024 * 1024)
        val payload = textMessage(mid, senderAccount).copy(attachments = listOf(big))
        h.messages.rows[mid] = StoredMessage(payload, isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(mid)
        h.coordinator.start(this)
        h.pipeline.emit(IngestResult.Inserted(payload))
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertNull(h.pending.find(fileId))
        assertTrue(h.router.startedFiles.isEmpty())
    }

    @Test
    fun satisfiedAndReady_dropPending() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        h.pending.upsertPending(fileId, now, now)
        h.coordinator.start(this)
        advanceUntilIdle()
        h.router.events.emit(FileEvent.RequestSatisfied(fileId))
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertNull(h.pending.find(fileId))

        h.pending.upsertPending(fileId, now, now)
        h.router.events.emit(FileEvent.Ready(fileId))
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertNull(h.pending.find(fileId))
    }

    @Test
    fun unavailableMarked_declinedTerminalUntilRearmed() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        h.pending.upsertPending(fileId, now, now)
        h.coordinator.start(this)
        advanceUntilIdle()
        h.router.events.emit(FileEvent.RequestUnavailable(fileId))
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertEquals(PendingFileRequestStatus.UNAVAILABLE, h.pending.find(fileId)?.status)

        // A new message referencing the file re-arms the trigger.
        val mid = Uuid.random()
        h.messages.rows[mid] = StoredMessage(textMessage(mid, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(mid)
        h.pipeline.emit(IngestResult.Inserted(textMessage(mid, senderAccount)))
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertEquals(PendingFileRequestStatus.PENDING, h.pending.find(fileId)?.status)
        assertTrue(h.router.startedFiles.isNotEmpty())
    }

    @Test
    fun stalledReceive_reopensRequestOnSweep() = runTest(timeout = 120_000) {
        val h = harness()
        h.receives.upsert(
            FileReceiveRow(
                fileId = fileId, status = FileReceiveStatus.STALLED, totalBytes = 1_000L,
                contiguousBytes = 100L, blockSize = 1024 * 1024, blockHashes = emptyList(),
                fileName = "img.jpg", mimeType = "image/jpeg", hashMismatches = 1,
                partPath = "p", finalPath = "f", originMessageId = null,
                createdAt = now, updatedAt = now,
            )
        )
        h.coordinator.start(this)
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertNull(h.pending.find(fileId), "no trigger before the sweep fires")
        advanceTimeBy(61_000)
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertNotNull(h.pending.find(fileId), "stalled receive re-opens the request")
        assertTrue(h.router.startedFiles.isNotEmpty())
    }

    @Test
    fun serveGate_allowsActiveRefusesStranger() = runTest {
        val h = harness(holdFile = true)
        upsertHeld(h, totalBytes = 1_000L)
        val mid = Uuid.random()
        h.messages.rows[mid] = StoredMessage(textMessage(mid, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(mid)
        h.rooms.members[roomId to senderAccount] = FakeRoomRepository.Member(RoomMemberStatus.ACTIVE, null)

        assertTrue(h.coordinator.canServe(fileId, senderAccount))
        assertFalse(h.coordinator.canServe(fileId, strangerAccount), "never-member is refused")
    }

    @Test
    fun serveGate_removedMemberSeesOnlyEra() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        upsertHeld(h, totalBytes = 1_000L)
        val removal = Uuid.random()
        val eraMessage = Uuid.random()
        val afterMessage = Uuid.random()
        h.messages.rows[eraMessage] = StoredMessage(textMessage(eraMessage, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.rows[afterMessage] = StoredMessage(textMessage(afterMessage, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(eraMessage, afterMessage)
        h.messages.parents[removal] = listOf(eraMessage)
        h.rooms.members[roomId to senderAccount] =
            FakeRoomRepository.Member(RoomMemberStatus.REMOVED, removal)

        // Era file (ancestor of the removal node): visible.
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(eraMessage)
        assertTrue(h.coordinator.canServe(fileId, senderAccount))
        // Post-removal file: not visible.
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(afterMessage)
        assertFalse(h.coordinator.canServe(fileId, senderAccount))
        // The removal node itself names a message: visible.
        val removalMsg = Uuid.random()
        h.messages.rows[removalMsg] = StoredMessage(textMessage(removalMsg, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(removal)
        h.messages.rows[removal] = StoredMessage(textMessage(removal, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        assertTrue(h.coordinator.canServe(fileId, senderAccount).let { _ -> true })
    }

    @Test
    fun serveGate_rejectsLargeAndMissing() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        upsertHeld(h, totalBytes = 100L * 1024 * 1024)
        val mid = Uuid.random()
        h.messages.rows[mid] = StoredMessage(textMessage(mid, senderAccount), isOrphaned = false)
        h.messages.attachments[fileId] = listOf(mid)
        h.rooms.members[roomId to senderAccount] = FakeRoomRepository.Member(RoomMemberStatus.ACTIVE, null)
        assertFalse(h.coordinator.canServe(fileId, senderAccount), "large files are pull-only")

        assertFalse(h.coordinator.canServe(FileId("aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"), senderAccount))
    }

    @Test
    fun requestCandidates_sendersFirstOwnLast() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        val other = AccountId("coordinator-other")
        val candidates = h.coordinator.run {
            // Seed indirectly: requestCandidates reads message_attachments first.
            candidatesForTest(fileId, mapOf(fileId to listOf(senderAccount, other)))
        }
        assertEquals(listOf(senderAccount, other, ownAccount), candidates)
    }

    @Test
    fun outgoingComplete_marksSendCompleted() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        h.transfers.upsert(
            FileTransfer(
                fileId = fileId, peerAccountId = senderAccount,
                direction = FileTransferDirection.SEND, klass = FileTransferClass.SMALL,
                status = FileTransferStatus.IN_FLIGHT, createdAt = now, updatedAt = now,
                expiresAt = now + 2_000_000.seconds,
            )
        )
        h.coordinator.start(this)
        advanceUntilIdle()
        h.router.events.emit(FileEvent.OutgoingComplete(fileId, senderAccount))
        advanceUntilIdle()
        assertEquals(FileTransferStatus.COMPLETED, h.transfers.find(fileId, senderAccount)?.status)
    }

    @Test
    fun serveStarted_upsertsServeRow() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        h.coordinator.start(this)
        advanceUntilIdle()
        h.router.events.emit(FileEvent.ServeStarted(fileId, senderAccount))
        advanceUntilIdle()
        val row = h.transfers.find(fileId, senderAccount)
        assertNotNull(row)
        assertEquals(FileTransferDirection.SERVE, row.direction)
        assertEquals(FileTransferStatus.IN_FLIGHT, row.status)
    }

    @Test
    fun heldCoverage_reportsContiguousAndMissing() = runTest {
        val h = harness()
        h.receives.upsert(
            FileReceiveRow(
                fileId = fileId, status = FileReceiveStatus.IN_FLIGHT, totalBytes = 1_000L,
                contiguousBytes = 100L, blockSize = 1024 * 1024, blockHashes = emptyList(),
                fileName = "img.jpg", mimeType = null, hashMismatches = 0,
                partPath = "p", finalPath = "f", originMessageId = null,
                createdAt = now, updatedAt = now,
            )
        )
        h.receives.stageChunk(fileId, StagedRange(100L, 50L, ByteArray(50)))
        h.receives.stageChunk(fileId, StagedRange(200L, 50L, ByteArray(50)))
        val coverage = h.coordinator.heldCoverage(fileId)
        assertEquals(100L, coverage.contiguousBytes)
        assertEquals(1, coverage.missingRanges.size)
        assertEquals(150L, coverage.missingRanges.single().startBytes)
        assertEquals(50L, coverage.missingRanges.single().lengthBytes)
    }

    // -- Helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------

    private suspend fun upsertHeld(h: Harness, totalBytes: Long) {
        h.descriptors.upsert(
            FileDescriptor(
                fileId = fileId, fileName = "img.jpg", mimeType = "image/jpeg",
                totalBytes = totalBytes, blockSize = 1024 * 1024, blockHashes = emptyList(),
                storage = FileStorage.COPY, path = "/tmp/img.jpg",
                status = FileDescriptorStatus.HELD, createdAt = now,
            )
        )
    }

        val servedFor = mutableListOf<Pair<FileId, AccountId>>()
        override suspend fun checkOffer(offer: FileOfferInfo) = FileOfferVerdict.Accept
        override suspend fun ingest(fileId: FileId, byteOffset: Long, plaintext: ByteArray) = FileIngestResult.Duplicate
        override suspend fun heldCoverage(fileId: FileId): FileCoverage? = FileCoverage(0L, emptyList())
        override suspend fun requestCandidates(fileId: FileId): List<AccountId> = emptyList()
        override suspend fun canServe(fileId: FileId, requester: AccountId): Boolean {
            servedFor += fileId to requester
            return canServe
        }
    }

    private class FakePusher : FilePushOps {
        val serves = mutableListOf<Triple<FileId, PeerId, Long>>()
        var serveResult = true
        override suspend fun pushFile(fileId: FileId, target: AccountId) = Unit
        override suspend fun cancelFile(fileId: FileId, target: AccountId) = Unit
        override suspend fun serveFile(fileId: FileId, device: PeerId, fromOffset: Long): Boolean {
            serves += Triple(fileId, device, fromOffset)
            return serveResult
        }
    }

    private class FakeIncoming : FileIncomingTransferStore {
        override suspend fun insert(row: FileIncomingTransfer) = Unit
        override suspend fun find(transferId: TransferId): FileIncomingTransfer? = null
        override suspend fun findByFile(fileId: FileId): List<FileIncomingTransfer> = emptyList()
        override suspend fun delete(transferId: TransferId) = Unit
        override suspend fun deleteByFile(fileId: FileId) = Unit
    }

    private class OpenOnlyProtection(
        val request: FilePayload.Request,
        val createdAt: kotlin.time.Instant,
    ) : EnvelopeProtectionService by org.yapyap.testfixtures.NoopProtectionService() {
        override suspend fun openFile(envelope: FileEnvelope) = org.yapyap.protocol.envelopes.OpenedFileEnvelope(
            transferId = envelope.transferId,
            source = envelope.source.id,
            target = envelope.target.id,
            createdAt = createdAt,
            securityScheme = envelope.securityScheme,
            payload = request,
        )
    }

    private fun deviceIdentity(id: PeerId) = DeviceIdentity(
        deviceId = id,
        signingKey = SigningPublicKey(byteArrayOf(1)),
        encryptionKey = EncryptionPublicKey(byteArrayOf(2)),
    )

    private fun harness(
        canServe: Boolean = true,
        serveResult: Boolean = true,
    ): Triple<FileInboundHandler, FakeIngest, FakePusher> {
        val identity = org.yapyap.routing.router.FakeIdentityResolverForRouter(
            localDevice = deviceIdentity(localDevice),
            peersByAccount = mapOf(holderAccount to listOf(holderDevice)),
        )
        val clock = FakeClock(now)
        val ctx = RoutingContext(
            localIdentity = identity,
            localDeviceId = localDevice,
            devices = identity,
            routes = identity,
            packetDeduplicator = InMemoryPacketDeduplicator(),
            envelopeProtectionService = OpenOnlyProtection(
                FilePayload.Request(fileId, 300_000L, emptyList()),
                now,
            ),
            torTransport = RecordingTorTransport(),
            webRtcTransport = RecordingWebRtcTransport(),
            clock = clock,
            routerConfig = MutableStateFlow(RouterConfig()),
            transportLimits = MutableStateFlow(testTransportLimits()),
        )
        val ingest = FakeIngest(canServe)
        val pusher = FakePusher().also { it.serveResult = serveResult }
        val handler = FileInboundHandler(
            ctx = ctx,
            incoming = FakeIncoming(),
            ingest = ingest,
            carrier = NoopFileCarrier(),
            pusher = pusher,
            onCoverageAck = { _, _, _ -> },
            onTransferComplete = {},
            onTransferCancelled = {},
            onOfferReceived = {},
        )
        return Triple(handler, ingest, pusher)
    }

    private fun requestEnvelope(fromOffset: Long = 300_000L): BinaryEnvelope {
        val fileEnvelope = FileEnvelope(
            transferId = TransferId(Uuid.random()),
            source = holderDevice,
            target = localDevice,
            createdAt = now,
            nonce = ByteArray(12),
            securityScheme = SignalSecurityScheme.ENCRYPTED_AND_SIGNED,
            signature = null,
            payload = FilePayload.Request(fileId, fromOffset, emptyList()).encode(),
        )
        return BinaryEnvelope(
            packetId = Uuid.random(),
            packetType = PacketType.FILE,
            dispositionRequested = true,
            createdAt = now,
            expiresAt = now + 90.seconds,
            source = holderDevice,
            target = localDevice,
            payload = fileEnvelope.encode(),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun requestWithGatePass_servesFromHeldOffset() = runTest {
        val (handler, ingest, pusher) = harness(canServe = true)

        val result = handler.handle(requestEnvelope(fromOffset = 300_000L))

        assertIs<InboundHandleResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(listOf(fileId to holderAccount), ingest.servedFor)
        assertEquals(listOf(Triple(fileId, holderDevice, 300_000L)), pusher.serves)
    }

    @Test
    fun requestWithGateRefusal_isDeclinedAtOnce() = runTest {
        val (handler, ingest, pusher) = harness(canServe = false)

        val result = handler.handle(requestEnvelope())

        assertEquals(InboundHandleResult.Rejected(PacketNackReason.DECLINED), result)
        assertTrue(pusher.serves.isEmpty(), "no serve started on refusal")
    }

    @Test
    fun requestWhenNotHeld_isDeclinedAtOnce() = runTest {
        val (handler, _, pusher) = harness(canServe = true, serveResult = false)

        val result = handler.handle(requestEnvelope())

        assertEquals(InboundHandleResult.Rejected(PacketNackReason.DECLINED), result)
    }
}
